submission.justification:
Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) at 30% wall coverage gives 35.3 PE/MeV from the current simulator (100k events). That is the highest light yield among the designs that pass the robustness requirement. Module-D1 gives more light (51.8 PE/MeV at 30%) but was excluded: 30% of modules failed 20-cycle thermal cycling (300K to 87K), far above the 5% limit, because the bonded thin light guide cracks on cooldown. Modules cannot be serviced after the cryostat is filled, so this rules D1 out. D3 failed 2% of modules, under the 5% limit, and D2 failed 0.5%. D3 yields about 1.4 to 1.5 times D2 at 15% and 30% coverage. 30% is the top of the permitted range and within the 30% feedthrough limit. Cold amplifiers are validated for all three designs, and the cryostat membrane and purity expectations impose no module-specific constraint.

Caveats: (1) D3's robustness margin is modest (2% against a 5% limit). D2 (0.5% failure, 26.4 PE/MeV at 30%) is the robust fallback if robustness should outweigh about 25% less light. (2) The thermal-cycling tests used 40 modules per design, and 2% and 0.5% are not whole-number counts at that size (0.8 and 0.2 modules), while 30% is 12 of 40. The D3 and D2 percentages should be checked against thermal_cycling_tests.md before design freeze, since that bears on the true D3 margin. I did not verify this against the source file. (3) The 2025 yield figure at 20% coverage (27 PE/MeV) is consistent with the current simulator. An earlier 27-29 PE/MeV interpolation was overstated; interpolation gives about 26. This does not change the ranking. (4) Design freeze is planned for Q3.
